text:
Sam: Kicking off a new staging soak focused on per-key burst behavior + per-org fallbacks. Goal: confirm we don't drop low-QPS keys when a few hot keys spike. loadgen scheduled for 2h.
Tara: Nice. What's the traffic profile? keys, qps, burst window?
Sam: Using loadgen v2 -> multi-key mix: 95% cold keys at 0.2 qps, 5% hot keys ramping to 250 qps each for short bursts. Ramp pattern: 5m warmup, 30m steady, 10m burst spikes every 6m. config snippet:
```
clients: 200
workload: mix
hot_key_ratio: 0.05
hot_key_peak_qps: 250
burst_window_ms: 1000
```
Mike: Important: run with both `per_key_enforcement=true` and `per_org_fallback=true` permutations. We saw earlier the fallback path was swallowing metrics.
Julia: Also please toggle `burst_smoothing` off for one run so we can compare raw enforcement vs smoothing.
Sam: Will run three variants: 1) per-key only, 2) per-key + org fallback, 3) per-key + org fallback + smoothing off. Expect ~2h each but can abort early if errors spike.
ops-bot: Noted: staging cluster has autoscaler cooldown 10m; if load hits, nodes may take ~4m to come up.
Tara: Add a synthetic client that replays cached prefix tokens to check cache bypass behavior. We had cache misses causing extra tokens charged.
Mike: Good call. Also enable `trace_id` logging on gateway for these runs so we can correlate throttles to ticketed requests. Use header `X-Trace-Id`.
Sam: Will add `X-Trace-Id: loadtest-<run>-<seq>` header. Also pushing a temporary dashboard panel: `rl.enforcement.per_key_denied` and `rl.enforcement.org_fallback_count`.
Julia: For dashboards, include p50/p95 latency for both accepted and 429 responses. Sometimes 429s are served fast and skew sLOs.
Sam: Agreed. Quick check: can someone confirm the quota service has the latest key->org mapping sync? Last sync showed a gap at 03:12 UTC yesterday.
Mike: I just kicked a resync job (`/services/quota/sync --force`) — logs look good, last sync at 1855123000.
Tara: If we hit unexplained 429s, check token metadata on requests: some clients were sending `x-api-key` header with trailing spaces and our canonicalization failed.
Sam: Oof. Will add a quick scrub step in the harness to trim whitespace.
ops-bot: deploy-bot reports: canary config for `quota-enforcer:v2.4.1` deployed to staging at 1855123220.
deploy-bot: :white_check_mark: canary rollout 10% -> 50% -> 100% scheduled, will pause on >1% 429 increase.
Julia: Reminder: for the run that disables smoothing, we should also flip on verbose enforcement metrics: `enf.debug=true`. Otherwise we won't know which rule triggered.
Mike: After first run, dump `quota-service` metrics: `curl http://staging-metrics/metrics | grep rl_enforcement` and attach to thread.
Tara: If anything looks off, also check `kv-cache.hit_rate` — prefix caching may be the reason hot keys aren't as hot as expected.
Sam: Starting run 1 now (per-key only). Will post interim after first 30m.
Mike: sgtm :thumbsup:
(30m later)
Sam: Interim: heatmap shows hot-key 1 peaked at 240 qps, enforcement triggered but denial rate low (~0.4%), org fallback not in play. p95 latency rose from 120 -> 360ms during bursts.
Julia: Can you paste a short log example for a denied request?
Sam: snippet:
```
[1855123605] TRACE loadtest-1 req_id=abc123 key=hotkey-42 action=DENY reason=burst_limit_exceeded enforcer=per_key
```
Tara: DENY reason is precise, good. Any mismatch between enforcement and billing counters?
Sam: Billing counters show ~1.1% extra token accounting vs enforcement denied; possible double-count when gateway retries.
Mike: Gateway retries should be disabled for 429s; check `retry_policy.max_retries` in gateway config.
Sam: It was 2 for connection errors, but `retry_on: 429` was accidentally present in one config. Fixing and restarting gateway.
ops-bot: gateway restart scheduled at 1855123608, cluster node 3 rotated.
Sam: Re-ran a short spike after fix: billing and enforcement now in sync within 0.05%.
Julia: Run 2 (per-key + org fallback) next? We're trying to confirm that org fallback preserves QoS for cold keys.
Sam: Starting run 2.
(1h later)
Sam: Observation: org_fallback engaged for ~0.6% of requests during peak; most were from small keys belonging to same org as hot keys. Latency for fallback served requests jumped to p95=720ms.
Tara: That latency spike is concerning. Could be routing through async fallback queue. Check `fallback.path=sync` vs `async`.
Mike: Also check DB read latencies for quota lookups — we saw a slow Redis shard earlier.
Sam: Redis shard rax-2 showed 95th latency 50ms during the run. Filed infra ticket if this repeats.
Julia: For the final run (smoothing off), let's also enable synthetic cross-org interference: add 10 other orgs with moderate hotkeys to see multi-org fairness.
Sam: Will do. One more item: can we add an ephemeral alert that fires if `rl.enforcement.org_fallback_count / rl.requests_total > 0.01` ? Would help catch regressions during rollouts.
Mike: Good idea. I'll add to staging alert rules with a 5m window.
Sam: Cool. Final note: please save all dashboards and attach time ranges for each run. I'll upload traces from `X-Trace-Id` to the ticket.
Tara: Thanks - nice catch on the gateway retry flag.
Julia: Great test. If smoothing is reducing latency but hiding enforcement, we need to decide console UX: show both raw denies and smoothed denies. Ops teams need both.
Sam: Noted — creating a small UX ticket for the rollouts page to surface both metrics.
Mike: I'll follow up with a short PR for the alert rule and the dashboard panel.
Sam: End-of-day summary will be posted once run 3 completes. :eyes:
